test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 1 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A 280 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 8 km/h (in same direction) in 16 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take this train to completely cross another 380 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 37 km/h?
solution:
**Given:**

A 280 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 8 km/h (in same direction) in 16 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take this train to completely cross another 380 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 37 km/h?

**Formula used:**

Relative speed in the same direction = Speed of train - Speed of man

Relative speed in the opposite direction = Speed of train + Speed of other train

Time to overtake = Distance / Relative speed

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train be x km/h.

Relative speed with respect to man = x - 8 km/h

Distance covered = 280 m = 0.28 km

⇒ Time taken to overtake man = 16 seconds = 16/3600 hours

⇒ 16/3600 = 0.28 / (x - 8)

⇒ (x - 8) = 0.28 × (3600 / 16)

⇒ (x - 8) = 63

⇒ x = 63 + 8

⇒ x = 71 km/h

Now, relative speed with respect to the other train = 71 + 37 km/h = 108 km/h

Distance to be covered = 280 m + 380 m = 660 m = 0.66 km

⇒ Time taken to cross = 0.66 / 108 hours

⇒ Time taken to cross = 0.66 × (3600 / 108) seconds

⇒ Time taken to cross ≈ 22 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
